settings.text: Going to the workshop was hands-down one of the best things I have ever done.
Pandas eat it. Schoolchildren used to be caned with it. But now prisoners at Lowdham Grange have found a surprising new use for bamboo — making bicycles out of it.
Bamboo bikes have that cool factor that excites them. There's maths and English in the programme — but it's built into design, creativity and bike mechanics.

settings.count_title: we publish what we can evidence, and say when we can't.
settings.count_body: Completion and confidence figures come from our own programme records and end-of-course surveys, dated at source. We don't publish return-on-investment figures or claim a reoffending outcome of our own; the Ministry of Justice research above is quoted as context, not as our result. Cohort sizes and site names change as programmes mobilise, so we count sites, not cohorts. We do not yet track what happens after release, we publish no carbon figure until a life-cycle assessment exists, and the CIC's first accounts are due in November 2026.

settings.ident_line: Bamboo Mobility Project CIC — a community interest company, not a registered charity. Registered UK learning provider, UKPRN 10098630, delivering two OCN London bespoke Level 2 courses. Activity since 2012; the CIC was incorporated in 2025. Workshops in London, Amersfoort, Toulouse and Brighton.
